correctness.rationale: Reconstructed both bipartition signature types: edge-vertex signatures are distinct/nonempty iff at most one original vertex is omitted; original signatures are distinct/nonempty iff the selected-edge graph has no order-one or order-two connected component. The equivalence yields an all-code polynomial. Labelled exponential formula removes components K1 and K2 exactly. A c-component selected-edge graph with all components order>=3 has c<=floor(n/3), edges >=n-c, with equality precisely a forest of floor(n/3) tree components. Cayley and multinomial counting give every minimum profile. Direct exhaustive checks cover all codes for n=3..5 and all selected-edge graphs for n=3..6 and independently verify coefficients.

value.rationale: The infinite family of one-subdivided cliques is a natural incidence-graph test case for open sensor identification. The theorem describes every feasible code and every polynomial coefficient, gives an exact sharp minimum, classifies equality as forest components of orders 3–5, and counts all optimal placements in explicit residue classes. Comparison to known ordinary total domination on the same graphs exhibits a real separation-cost gap, making this a substantive structural refinement rather than a routine isolated number.
